Qinah leḤurban Gan Aden, an eco-lament by Richard Kaplan (2003)

tei:bibl.tei:title: קִינָה לְחֻרְבַּן גַּן עֵדֶן
Qinah leḤurban Gan Aden, an eco-lament by Richard Kaplan (2003)
tei:bibl.tei:author: Richard Kaplan
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: Cantor Richard Kaplan, z”l, composed this qinah (lament) for Tishah b’Av about the destruction of the earth. Gan Aden of course is the Garden of Eden, both a place and a time. It is the imagined birthplace of all life and species, and an echo of the time when the real Earth was untrammeled. Ḥurban usually refers to the destruction of the First and Second Temples, but here to the Temple of the Earth, which the Jewish Temple was meant to represent according to midrash.

The song articulates the voice of Gaia, the Earth, embodied in Richard’s plaintive voice. Richard died on the first day of Sukkkot [in 2021], and thinking about him has made me want so much to hear his voice, calling us to truth.
“Kinah Lekhurban Gan Eden” was written by Richard Kaplan and first published as the fourth track to his album Life of the Worlds: Journeys in Jewish Sacred Music (2003).

tei:note.tei:p: For the Mishkan as microcosm and the Temple as omphalos, find Bamidbar Rabbah Naso 12:4.
Also, his birthday in the Jewish calendar.
